elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence limits exercise to "no more than once per year" — a calendar/annual framing rather than the preferred "once in any 12-month period" rolling limit; the drafter targeted the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted language requires only "at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice," and does not require the notice to be in writing.
No business-hours restriction appears anywhere in the rendered operative language; Subsection 11.3 as amended is silent on timing of day.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The investigation remains one IBM conducts itself ("IBM may exercise its investigation and verification rights"); no independent auditor is required.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No auditor is designated and no confidentiality undertaking for audit personnel is added.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference is inserted; the investigation right's location is unconstrained.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Cost shifting is set at the fallback threshold: "unless it establishes an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%)".

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: No prohibition on access to Customer systems is added; the redline addresses only frequency, notice and cost.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "IBM may exercise its investigation and verification rights under this Subsection 11.3 no more than once per year".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: "and only upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice to Customer" — an unconditional prior-notice precondition to exercising the investigation right.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "IBM will bear all costs of each such investigation unless it establishes an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%)" — cost sits with Vendor, shifting only above the 10% threshold.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: a single inserted sentence supplies all three fallback elements (once per year, at least 15 days' prior notice, Vendor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%) in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred level is not reached — no 30-day written notice, business-hours limit, independent confidential auditor, off-site preference, 5% cost threshold, or no-system-access prohibition. That is acceptable because the claimed target is the fallback, but if the drafter later wants the preferred level these six items must be added expressly.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tails, procedures, or extras beyond the three selected elements; existing Customer-favourable language (including the p0137 attempt-to-notify sentence) is retained.

Intent preserved: the new limits are scoped to "investigation and verification rights under this Subsection 11.3" and do not disturb the emergency/legal-requirement carve-out in p0137, which governs the separate remedial activities under 11.3(a)/(b) rather than the investigation itself. Watch-item only: if IBM reads 11.3(a)/(b) as within the amended sentence, it may argue the emergency carve-out overrides the 15-day notice — a clarifying "notwithstanding the emergency exception in Subsection 11.3(c), the investigation right requires 15 days' prior notice" would remove the ambiguity, though it is not required for fallback completeness.

Residual gap the drafter should be aware of (not a checklist failure): p0138's open-ended obligation to provide "all relevant information ... at IBM's request" is left untouched and is not covered by the new Subsection 11.3 limits, so IBM retains an unlimited, unnoticed information-demand channel outside the audit cap. The rationale cites p0138 as a driver but the operative edit does not reach it.

The cost trigger mirrors the checklist wording ("underpayment ... exceeding ten percent (10%)"), so it is met as drafted; note commercially that an AUP-violation investigation rarely produces an "underpayment," meaning IBM will in practice always bear cost — a Customer-favourable outcome, not a defect.
